title: Navy band service 1942-45 and return to New Orleans
summary: He played in the US Navy band in California and McAlester, Oklahoma from 1942 to 1945, then returned to his job at the Athletic Club and spot jobs.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years

blocks.x: while he was in the service, did you keep playing then? I mean. I kept playing, but I was. Did you work with them, through that period? There's different bands, but I played with the United States Navy Band in the Navy for three years. Yeah? Uh. What was that, here? Well, that's in, uh, Los Alameda, California and MacAlestock, Oklahoma. We switched over there. Uh-huh. Was
that, uh, musicians from New Orleans fighting there? No, mixing, all, all over. Yeah. I'm
all over. All parts. Cleveland, New York, Chicago. Where was that, uh, that picture you had
there with, uh, what's his name? Nelson. With Nelson? Yeah. Well, that was in, uh,

MacAlestock, Oklahoma. And he was traveling with the band then? He was with the band. He was playing with the band. Yeah. With the Navy Band. Was there any more New Orleans musicians in that band? In that band, Larry. Hubbert Larry? No, no, not Hubbert Larry. Jimmy Larry. Oh, no. Jimmy Larry. Oh, no. Jimmy Larry. Any more besides that? No, that was the only, we was the only three from New Orleans in that band. What band was that, the proper name of that band? The New Orleans, the United States Neighbor Band. Oh, right. When we, when we moved to MacAlister, we was the MacAlister, United States, uh, Neighbor
MacAlister Band. Yeah. And that was, that was when Sheik was in that music school that you

was traveling with his band? No, no, Sheik went in the music school after that. I got a discharge in 45. Oh, yeah. I played in the Navy Band from 42 to 45. Yeah. What, what happened when you came out? When I came out, I went back to the club, that's in Missouri over there, New Orleans Athletic Club. I mean, what, what band did you play with after that? Oh, there's a different band, there's Spot Jobs, Spot Jobs. Uh-huh. See, I couldn't play no study band because I had a job, I was working, I had to play Spot Jobs. So, where were you working? New Orleans Athletic Club. Oh, yeah, that's right, yeah. Masseur. Masseur, I worked there 38 years. Yeah. Count me three years out of the Navy. Uh-huh. Let's think, there's anything else we haven't covered.
I believe you played in the Anderson Minor Band. I've seen you work with Anderson Minor Band.

Anderson Minor, I played with him too. Were you regular with him or you? No, just played Spot Jobs with Anderson Minor. Carnival Parades. Carnival Parades. Yeah. Different thing, you know. You worked, I believe, with Lawrence Tucker. I worked with Lawrence Tucker. Was that a regular band? That was a regular band, but that was back in 1928, in 27, you know. Who was in that band? Well, Melvin Frank was in that band, Clannette. Yeah. I was the trombone player, Eddie Summers. Bill Hamilton, he was banjo. Yeah. And Gus Green was the bass player, along with the trumpet. And, uh, Bill Hamilton was the banjo player.
